articles.title: Google Expands Guided AI Tools for Schools
articles.excerpt: Google is bringing Guided Learning to Classroom and Search while adding new controls for K-12 accounts and more AI training for educators.
articles.content:
Google announced a collection of education-focused AI updates on November 3, 2026, led by the global launch of Guided Learning in Google Classroom. The company is also bringing Guided Learning capabilities to Google Search.

## Tools Designed for Learning

The updates focus on using AI to support the learning process rather than simply returning answers. Google said it is also changing controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search when they are used through K-12 student accounts.

## Training and Research

Alongside the product changes, Google announced new research, additional Google.org funding, and an expansion of AI training for educators. These efforts reflect a broader push to help schools introduce generative AI with clearer oversight and learning-specific design.

For students and educators, the announcement is significant because it places AI tutoring and guidance directly inside tools already used in classrooms. The practical impact will depend on how schools configure the products and how teachers incorporate them into coursework.

articles.title: GitHub Reworks Software Development Around AI Agents
articles.excerpt: GitHub Universe 2026 introduced multi-repository agent projects, continuous sessions, automated workflows, and deeper AI code review.
articles.content:
At GitHub Universe on October 28, GitHub presented a vision of software development in which developers direct work while AI agents implement and verify changes across the delivery process.

## From Code Generation to Completed Work

GitHub introduced Copilot projects for running managed agent work across multiple repositories in parallel. Session continuity is designed to let developers follow the same cloud agent session from the GitHub app, Visual Studio Code, the command line, or the web.

Copilot automations can respond to repository events or schedules for tasks such as issue triage and code review. GitHub also announced a Max mode for Copilot code review, intended for deeper analysis of changes where high-severity bugs are a concern.

## Infrastructure Changes

The company said it is also rebuilding parts of the infrastructure beneath GitHub. Its stated principles for Git architecture include simpler primitives, separation of storage and compute, and less coordination overhead. The announcements show how quickly AI agents are moving from optional coding assistants toward integrated software-delivery systems.

articles.title: A Shared Robots.txt Signal Aims to Simplify AI Training Choices
articles.excerpt: OpenAI says it will honor a common signal that lets website operators communicate generative-AI training preferences to multiple providers.
articles.content:
OpenAI announced on October 30 that it plans to honor a shared robots.txt signal for foundational generative-AI training preferences. The proposal is meant to give publishers and website operators one way to communicate their choice to participating AI providers.

## Fewer Provider-Specific Rules

Website operators have generally needed to identify individual crawlers and maintain separate directives for different providers. A common signal could reduce that maintenance burden while making preferences easier to understand and apply.

OpenAI said the shared signal will not replace its existing crawler controls, which will continue to operate. The company expects to implement the new signal in the coming months and said it will provide more details before deployment.

The work builds on discussions in the Internet Engineering Task Force's AI Preferences group. Because the effort is voluntary, its broader effect will depend on adoption by AI companies, publishing platforms, and website operators.

articles.title: IBM and UChicago Report a Verifiable Quantum-Advantage Experiment
articles.excerpt: Researchers used 70 logical qubits and an error-detecting circuit design to run a computation they say is beyond practical classical simulation.
articles.content:
IBM and University of Chicago researchers announced a quantum-computing experiment on July 30 that they say meets two difficult goals at once: exceeding practical classical simulation and providing evidence that the quantum result is accurate.

## Seventy Logical Qubits

The experiment encoded 70 logical qubits and ran 2,415 logical two-qubit operations along with 468 logical T gates. IBM reported that encoding reduced effective logical error rates to one-tenth of the underlying physical error rates.

The team used a structured alternative to random-circuit sampling that allows errors to be detected while retaining the computational hardness needed for the benchmark. According to IBM, the quantum computation took about 15 minutes, while leading classical approaches faced prohibitive runtimes.

The researchers released the circuits and results publicly, and their associated paper describes the verification method. Independent analysis and future replication will help establish how the result fits into the continuing debate over useful and trustworthy quantum advantage.

articles.title: NASA Tests a New Processor Built for Autonomous Spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA and Microchip's radiation-hardened system-on-a-chip is undergoing thermal, shock, radiation, and performance testing at JPL.
articles.content:
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory is testing a next-generation High Performance Spaceflight Computing processor designed to bring substantially more computing power to spacecraft.

## Computing in Harsh Environments

Spacecraft processors must tolerate radiation, extreme temperature changes, launch forces, and years without physical maintenance. JPL's campaign includes radiation, thermal, shock, functional, and simulated landing tests. NASA reported in May that early indications showed the processor operating at roughly 500 times the performance of radiation-hardened chips currently in use.

The palm-sized system-on-a-chip includes processor cores, computational accelerators, networking, memory, and input/output capabilities. It was developed through a partnership between NASA, JPL, and Microchip Technology.

More capable onboard computers could let future spacecraft analyze scientific data faster and respond autonomously when communication delays make immediate instructions from Earth impossible. NASA expects the technology to support orbiters, planetary rovers, crewed habitats, and deep-space missions after certification.

articles.title: HackRPI 2027 Greetings
articles.excerpt: Greetings HackRPI Hackers 2027! Here is our message to you.
articles.content:
### Welcome Hackers!

HackRPI 2026 is Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute's 13th annual intercollegiate hackathon hosted by students for students. Starting at noon on Saturday, November 7th, teams of 1-4 people have 24 hours to build and submit projects relating to our theme, In The Clouds. 

After submitting their projects, participants showcase their work in front of professors, industry professionals, and fellow students.

### In The Clouds: 

Soar to new heights at our 13th annual hackathon. This year’s theme challenges you to design projects that take flight—whether literally or figuratively. Elevate existing solutions to high peaks or even create something new with emerging technologies. After all, the sky’s the limit (or is it?!). 

### Our Goal 

Our goal is to inspire and challenge innovators, creators, developers, and entrepreneurs in New York's Tech Valley and beyond. All students from all schools are welcome to participate, regardless of their major or experience level. Whether you're a seasoned hacker or a first-time participant, HackRPI is the perfect opportunity to learn new skills, meet new people, and have fun!
